paragraphs: Friend, look at who is on that hill. Jesus has the rulers sneering, the soldiers mocking and a crowd watching, and every one of them says some version of "save Yourself!" (Luke 23:37). He could have. Instead He stays, and the first words we hear from the cross are "Father, forgive them, for they do not know what they are doing." (Luke 23:34). That's the big idea, baker: Jesus doesn't get pushed into this. He stays on that cross for the very people who are mocking Him.

Now look at the man hanging next to Him. He admits, "We are punished justly," and then he asks one thing: "Jesus, remember me when You come into Your kingdom!" (Luke 23:41-42). No good résumé, no time to fix anything, no cookies to bring. Jesus answers, "Truly I tell you, today you will be with Me in Paradise." (Luke 23:43). So if you ever feel too far gone or too late, this man says come as you are, because you can't earn it and you don't have to.

Then the sun goes dark, the temple veil is torn down the middle, and Jesus says, "Father, into Your hands I commit My Spirit." (Luke 23:44-46). Even a Roman centurion gives glory to God and says, "Surely this was a righteous man." (Luke 23:47). This is why my ovens stay ready, friend: the One who stayed on that cross is the One we're all baking for. Keep that apron on, because this story is NOT done.
